newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa slumps as funds sell, stops hit.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa slumps as funds sell, stops hit.

text.p: CSCE cocoa prices slumped to their lowest level in more than a month ahead of midday, battered by successive waves of heavy speculative liquidation, market soureces said.
In what traders said was mainly a technical breakdown, the market tumbled some $50 a tonne basis the July contract after skidding through support at $1,440 and then $1,410.
"We're getting what appears to be some long liquidation from the funds," said one trader. "The market broke some uptrend lines it had been following since early April."
Benchmark July futures were down $47 per tonne as of 1137 EDT, to $1,408, after briefly sinking to a low of $1,397.

The selling intensified as the market worked its way lower, with scale-down trade buying offering only meager support. July futures took out a crucial downside objective at $1,410, a double chart bottom set in early April.
A key trendline was also crossed on London's July futures at 1019 stg a tonne, traders said.
Volume was moderate into the decline, reaching an estimated 4,083 lots as of 1100 EDT.
Traders said the market's swift collapse set the stage for a test of two-month lows at $1,365 basis July.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
